newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Pro7 TV station sees hefty interest in IPO.
newsitem.headline: German Pro7 TV station sees hefty interest in IPO.

text.p: Television broadcaster Pro Sieben (Pro7), which plans this summer to become the first German TV station with a stock market listing, expects sizeable interest in its initial public offering (IPO), Pro7 chairman Gerog Koffler told the German weekly Focus magazine.

Pro Sieben's flotation of preference shares, which aims to raise one billion marks, is scheduled for the midddle of June and Kofler hopes the stock will begin trade on July 7, Focus said in its weekend edition.
"I think demand for our shares will be 10 times as much as the offering," Kofler told the magazine.

He said that around half a million private investors had already inquired about Pro7 shares via a special hotline, and said many large investors had been impressed by what he called the firm's "success story".
Focus said that according to its own calculations, Pro7 prefence shares could be offered at between 65 and 70 marks each.

Kofler said there was a good chance that Pro Sieben would outperform Germany's wider DAX index of leading shares, saying that from 1997 onwards the firm expected to be paying appropriate dividends to shareholders.
The broadcaster's chairman said he expected ordinary shares in Pro Sieben would also be trading by the year 2000.
For the first quarter of 1997, Kofler told Focus that Pro7's performance had been "brilliant" and was significantly better than a year ago. He did not give any definitive figures.

Pro7 said last month that its gross advertising income for the first quarter was 18 percent higher than the previous year at 641 million marks, putting it among the top three German television stations in terms of growth.
